messages:
Jon R.: Quick heads-up — since rolling r3379 (phase-aware scheduling tweaks) to canary we've seen a 6-8% increase in p99 gen latency on the openai-large bench and a small uptick in token-cost. Noticed it right after the kernel affinity changes landed. stack: serving/runtime scheduler -> batcher -> kernel-selection.
Anika S.: ugh. saw similar in infra-today channel. Any flamegraph / profile pointers? :eyes:
Priya K.: I captured a short perf trace from canary node 10. Top-level looks like more frequent kernel_fallback and memcpy spikes during the first decode tokens. Prefill seems to be taking larger batches and starving the decode-stage small batches.
perf-bot: perf-sample 1719876601 openai-large canary-10
perf-bot: hotfunctions:
```
kernel_fallback 32.5%
kv_cache_miss_handler 18.2%
cuda_memcpy_async 14.1%
prefill_batch_merge 9.8%
decode_queue_wait 8.7%
```
Marco L.: That matches my adhoc microbench. Phase-aware routing was letting prefill batches grow aggressively (since they hit the latency SLO for their phase) which increased kernel choices to larger-window kernels; then decode bursts land on the wrong kernels and fall back.
Jon R.: So it's both kernel selection (fallbacks) and queue policy (batch formation). I think the token-budget target math also got tweaked in r3379 — effective token_budget for decode-phase went up from 64->96 because of the new combined budget smoothing.
Anika S.: If decode's effective budget is larger, it waits to fill more before dispatching => higher tail. We should try forcing decode target down to 48 in canary to test. Small decode batches are latency-sensitive.
Priya K.: Agree. Proposed quick experiments:
1) Split prefill and decode into two separate queue lanes (mark requests by stage) so prefill batching heuristics don't influence decode.
2) Temporarily reduce decode token_budget to 48.
3) Add a short KV-cache warmup penalty: if kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.85, prioritize decode for the next 3 tokens.
Marco L.: I like 1 and 2. 3 is neat but more invasive. We can A/B it behind a flag.
Jon R.: Also consider kernel-selection hinting: when a decode batch arrives and the model kv cache indicates small sequence delta, prefer low-latency kernel even if that kernel is not the strictly highest throughput. We already surface kernel metadata in the batch descriptor. Could add kernel_hint: "latency_prefer".
Anika S.: Kernel hinting + queue separation seems minimal-risk. I'll prototype queue lane split + decode_budget override in a patch.
perf-bot: abtest candidate created: ab-1719876670 queue-split + decode-48 flag enabled on canary-10
Priya K.: I pushed a small patch to reduce decode budget and to short-circuit batch merge for decode-stage:
```
// scheduler config tweak
stages.decode.token_budget: 48
stages.decode.merge_window_ms: 4  // previously 12
queue.split_by_stage: true
```
Marco L.: Running microbench now. Early signal: p50 steady, p99 on openai-large dropped ~4% after decode budget change but kernel_fallback still at ~20%.
Jon R.: Good partial win. Means decode dispatch helped but fallback remains. That points to kernel selection mismatch on handoff. Maybe prefill forces kernel choice at batch formation time and decode inherits it.
Anika S.: I'll update the batch descriptor to carry kernel_hint separate per sub-stage (prefill_kernel_hint vs decode_kernel_hint). Then the kernel selector can respect decode hint when decode tokens are present. Will get a draft today.
Priya K.: Also let's capture a microtrace where we force decode_kernel_hint=latency and compare cublas vs our custom attention kernel hotpaths. If latency-prefers reduce memcpy/cold path calls, we should see kernel_fallback drop.
perf-bot: trace-collected 1719876762 canary-10 decode-latency-hint
perf-bot: hotfunctions after hint:
```
kernel_fallback 8.9%
cuda_memcpy_async 9.4%
kv_cache_miss_handler 16.2%
prefill_batch_merge 7.1%
```
Marco L.: Wow, kernel_fallback dropped a lot when decode was allowed to pick latency kernels. p99 improved ~7% in this run vs baseline.
Jon R.: Great. So plan:
- Short term (today): keep queue split + decode token_budget=48 in canary, enable decode_kernel_hint=latency. Roll to more canaries if p99 stays within target.
- Medium: make kernel_hint plumbing robust and add flagging to prefer smaller-kernel paths for decode-phase by default for latency-tier customers.
- Long term: more adaptive token budgets based on observed kv_cache_hit_rate and token-latency SLO.
Anika S.: I'll open the PR for kernel_hint + queue-split, include perf traces in the description. Assign to Marco for benching.
Priya K.: I'll run broader regression suite across small and large models to ensure no throughput regressions for batch-centric workloads.
Jon R.: Thanks all. If anyone sees regressions on other tests, ping here @channel. :thumbsup:
Marco L.: noted — will post bench links in an hour with CI graphs.
perf-bot: action: PR #4182 created by Anika S. description: "init-split queue + decode latency hints"
Jon R.: leaving canary monitoring on overnight. If nothing surprising by tomorrow morning, we'll promote this change and keep the kernel affinity toggle available as rollback.
Anika S.: ack.
